\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{طلوع} (tulū)}{طلوع (tulū)}]{\ur{طلوع} (tulū) — the rising (of the sun)}

\label{lesson:UR-C432-tulu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for mist, then the Urdu for to let up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{طلوع}}
\textbf{\ur{طلوع}} — \emph{tulū} — \textquotedblleft{}the rising (of the sun)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سورج} \ur{چھ} \ur{بجے} \ur{طلوع} \ur{ہوتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sūraj chhe baje tulū hotā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The sun rises at six.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{طلوع}} (\emph{tulū}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ṭulūʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}rising\textquotedblright{}; with \textbf{\ur{ہونا}} it means the sun comes up.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tulū}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tulū}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sūraj chhe baje tulū hotā hai.} — The sun rises at six.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for mist, then the Urdu for to let up, then say \emph{tulū} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{طلوع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The rising (of the sun)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{غروب} (ghurūb)}{غروب (ghurūb)}]{\ur{غروب} (ghurūb) — the setting (of the sun)}

\label{lesson:UR-C432-ghurub}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to let up, then the Urdu for the rising (of the sun).

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{افق} (ufuq)}{افق (ufuq)}]{\ur{افق} (ufuq) — the horizon}

\label{lesson:UR-C432-ufuq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for the rising (of the sun), then the Urdu for the setting (of the sun).

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اجالا} (ujālā)}{اجالا (ujālā)}]{\ur{اجالا} (ujālā) — daylight; the first light}

\label{lesson:UR-C432-ujala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for the horizon, then the Urdu for the glow of sunset.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اجالا}}
\textbf{\ur{اجالا}} — \emph{ujālā} — \textquotedblleft{}daylight; the first light\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{صبح} \ur{چھ} \ur{بجے} \ur{اجالا} \ur{ہوتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{subah chhe baje ujālā hotā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It gets light at six in the morning.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اجالا}} (\emph{ujālā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ujālā}, \textquotedblleft{}bright\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{ujjvālaka}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 1673).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Pure and Genuine to Sunrise and Sunset}

\label{lesson:UR-R432-review-426-432}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for unmixed and authentic.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item unmixed, authentic, adulteration, to rub, to polish
  \item a size, loose, an outfit, a handkerchief, to look good (on someone)
  \item a drop, to pour (of rain), a spell of rain, steam, to gather (of clouds)
  \item moisture, a chill, the cold season, to shrink, to go stiff
  \item the temperature (in everyday talk), a degree (of temperature), to be burning hot, airless heat, to fan (someone)
  \item a rain cloud, to be surrounded, to spread over, mist, to let up
  \item the rising (of the sun), the setting (of the sun), the horizon, the glow of sunset, daylight
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Unmixed? (\textbf{\ur{خالص}}, \emph{khālis}.) Authentic? (\textbf{\ur{اصلی}}, \emph{aslī}.) Adulteration? (\textbf{\ur{ملاوٹ}}, \emph{milāvaṭ}.) To rub? (\textbf{\ur{رگڑنا}}, \emph{ragaṛnā}.) To polish? (\textbf{\ur{چمکانا}}, \emph{chamkānā}.) A size? (\textbf{\ur{سائز}}, \emph{sāiz}.) Loose? (\textbf{\ur{ڈھیلا}}, \emph{ḍhīlā}.) An outfit? (\textbf{\ur{پوشاک}}, \emph{poshāk}.) A handkerchief? (\textbf{\ur{رومال}}, \emph{rūmāl}.) To look good (on someone)? (\textbf{\ur{سجنا}}, \emph{sajnā}.) A drop? (\textbf{\ur{بوند}}, \emph{būṅd}.) To pour (of rain)? (\textbf{\ur{برسنا}}, \emph{barasnā}.) A spell of rain? (\textbf{\ur{جھڑی}}, \emph{jhaṛī}.) Steam? (\textbf{\ur{بھاپ}}, \emph{bhāp}.) To gather (of clouds)? (\textbf{\ur{امڈنا}}, \emph{umaḍnā}.) Moisture? (\textbf{\ur{نمی}}, \emph{namī}.) A chill? (\textbf{\ur{ٹھنڈ}}, \emph{ṭhanḍ}.) The cold season? (\textbf{\ur{جاڑا}}, \emph{jāṛā}.) To shrink? (\textbf{\ur{سکڑنا}}, \emph{sikuṛnā}.) To go stiff? (\textbf{\ur{اکڑنا}}, \emph{akaṛnā}.) The temperature (in everyday talk)? (\textbf{\ur{پارہ}}, \emph{pārā}.) A degree (of temperature)? (\textbf{\ur{ڈگری}}, \emph{ḍigrī}.) To be burning hot? (\textbf{\ur{تپنا}}, \emph{tapnā}.) Airless heat? (\textbf{\ur{حبس}}, \emph{habs}.) To fan (someone)? (\textbf{\ur{جھلنا}}, \emph{jhalnā}.) A rain cloud? (\textbf{\ur{ابر}}, \emph{abr}.) To be surrounded? (\textbf{\ur{گھرنا}}, \emph{ghirnā}.) To spread over? (\textbf{\ur{چھانا}}, \emph{chhānā}.) Mist? (\textbf{\ur{دھند}}, \emph{dhund}.) To let up? (\textbf{\ur{تھمنا}}, \emph{thamnā}.) The rising (of the sun)? (\textbf{\ur{طلوع}}, \emph{tulū}.) The setting (of the sun)? (\textbf{\ur{غروب}}, \emph{ghurūb}.) The horizon? (\textbf{\ur{افق}}, \emph{ufuq}.) The glow of sunset? (\textbf{\ur{شفق}}, \emph{shafaq}.) Daylight? (\textbf{\ur{اجالا}}, \emph{ujālā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
